_comment: EXT-63 SMOKE, arm 9 — arm 4 (rxcb) + a00 ANCHORED TO THE COD GIM.  The ROOT-CAUSE
VALIDATION arm (docs/HANDOFF_ext_cb_iono_level.md, ROOT CAUSE section).
Measured cause of DEFECT 2: the 61 stations' receiver C1C-C2W GF biases have mean
~-5 ns (-15 slant-TECU) and clustered spread (std ~21 TECU).  rx_code_bias_datum's
zero-MEAN convention forces that mean into the confounded direction = the field level
(field-vs-GIM at its own IPPs: -13.5 TECU).  The level defect is an S-basis realization
mismatch, so the fix is a FRAME CHOICE: adopt COD's iono level by anchoring a00 to the
GIM's area-weighted global mean (32.24 TECU at DOY-129 00:00) through the EXISTING
per-epoch mean-reverting a00 prior (NetworkRunContext ~:1309 — clim anchor folded
EVERY epoch in information space, so it stands against the walk, unlike an
initial-only prior).  sigma 2.0 -> info 0.25/ep, SOFT: the border stays non-empty and
the field remains data-shaped; only the confounded LEVEL direction is informed.
PREDICTION (stated before the run):
- a00 ignites and HOLDS in ~28-33 (equilibrium offset vs the ~1 TECU/ep walk pump is
~pump/info = ~4 TECU at sigma 2; if it sags below ~28, tighten sigma to 1).
- sh_health gate: a00_in_band stays 1 all 20 epochs (arm 4: left band at ep 8).
- The OPEN question this arm answers: does the DEG-1 DIPOLE (30-40 TECU rms_deg1,
control 8-12) survive a correct level?  The dipole is attributed to the CLUSTERED
rx-bias spread, not the mean, so prediction is PARTIAL persistence — if it collapses
too, the level and dipole shared one mechanism; if it persists, the next lever is
the per-LOS iono x_lin seed (charged with rx bias at birth).
- rxcb prires family may get louder (states now fight the zero-mean datum) — expected,
MEASURE-ONLY.
20 epochs is inside ignition: LEVEL + gate wiring read only, no settled-science claim.
